/-!
# Erdős Problem 918

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/918](https://www.erdosproblems.com/918)
- [ErHa68b] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., On chromatic number of infinite graphs. (1968), 83--98.
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
-/

universe u

open scoped Cardinal Ordinal

namespace Erdos918

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_2$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every
subgraph on $\aleph_1$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
-- Formalisation note: source material [ErHa68b] uses only induced subgraphs
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ₁), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that
every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
-- Formalisation note: `ω` here is `Ordinal.omega0`, from `open scoped Ordinal`, as in 623.lean.
-- It is the fixed first infinite ordinal, not a variable: `variants.erdos_hajnal` settles every
-- finite `k`, and `ℵ_ω` is the limit of that family, so this asks the single next case.
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ_ ω), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_2$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every
subgraph on $\aleph_1$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
-- Formalisation note: for the `≤ ℵ₀` direction this is the same question as `parts.i`, not a
-- separate one. Every subgraph on `W` is contained in the induced subgraph on `W`, so its
-- chromatic cardinal is no larger; and the top subgraph induced on `W` has `coe` equal to
-- `G.induce W`. So the two quantifications are equivalent and the answers cannot differ. The
-- `= ℵ₀` pair below is genuinely different, because an edgeless subgraph has chromatic
-- cardinal `1`, and that is the source's own reason for the impossibility there.
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ₁), H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a graph with $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ vertices and chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that
every subgraph on $\aleph_\omega$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq\aleph_0$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.all_subgraphs.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ (ω + 1) ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ_ ω), H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- A question of Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal [ErHa68b], who proved that for every finite $k$
there is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_k$ vertices where each subgraph on
less than $\aleph_k$ vertices has chromatic number $\leq \aleph_0$. -/
-- Formalisation note: the source is missing the assumption that the graph have ℵₖ vertices
-- which can be found in [ErHa68b]
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.erdos_hajnal (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : ∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V),
    #V = ℵ_ k ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₁ ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W < ℵ_ k), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal ≤ ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the first question with induced subgraphs. -/
-- Formalisation note: the source states the impossibility for general subgraphs, in a
-- parenthetical, "assuming subgraph and not induced subgraph was intended". It does not
-- assert it for induced subgraphs, and the argument for the general case does not carry
-- over: an induced subgraph on `W` has chromatic cardinal at least that of any subgraph
-- on `W`, so the edgeless-subgraph argument is unavailable here.
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.i :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (W : Set V) (_ : #W = ℵ₁), (G.induce W).chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the first question with all subgraphs. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.i :
    ¬∃ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V), #V = ℵ_ 2 ∧ G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 2 ∧
      ∀ (H : G.Subgraph) (_ : #H.verts = ℵ₁), H.coe.chromaticCardinal = ℵ₀ := by
  sorry

/-- In [Er69b] the questions are stated with $= \aleph_0$ rather than $\leq\aleph_0$. This is
a likely typo since it can be shown that no such graph exists in this case.

This is the second question with induced subgraphs. -/

@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0.parts.ii :

This is the second question with all subgraphs. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_918.variants.eq_aleph_0_all_subgraphs.parts.ii :

end Erdos918

findings.description: The theorem asserts unconditionally, assuming only `0 < k`, the existence of a graph with exactly `ℵ_ k` vertices, chromatic cardinal `ℵ₁`, and countably colorable induced subgraphs of every smaller size. The cited result with these exact aleph cardinalities assumes the generalized continuum hypothesis. The formalisation note imports the vertex-cardinality condition from that conditional result without importing its hypothesis. The unconditional Theorem 2 in the paper instead uses successors of iterated powerset cardinalities, which cannot simply be identified with `ℵ_ k` without the relevant cardinal-arithmetic assumptions.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Hajnal, On chromatic number of infinite graphs (1968), §3, Corollary 1, p. 86, explicitly begins: “Assume G.C.H.” It then gives, for every ξ and 1 < k < ω, a graph of size ω_{ξ+k}, chromatic number ω_{ξ+1}, and chromatic number at most ω_ξ on subgraphs of size at most ω_{ξ+k−1}. Taking ξ = 0 gives the claimed finite-k result. The introduction, p. 83, also explicitly distinguishes the GCH-dependent conclusion from the unconditional Theorem 2. https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1968-04.pdf . Lambie-Hanson–Rinot, §2.1 of https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929, likewise states the k = 2 Erdős–Hajnal result with the hypothesis `2^ℵ₀ = ℵ₁`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit GCH hypothesis and include it in the docstring, for example `(hGCH : ∀ o : Ordinal.{u}, (2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ (ℵ_ o) = ℵ_ (o + 1))`, retaining the existing conclusion. The extra k = 1 case is harmless and has a direct proof using the complete graph on ℵ₁ vertices. Alternatively, formulate the unconditional iterated-powerset version of Theorem 2 with its actual cardinalities and chromatic-number conclusion.

status_issues.source_status: The first question has a relative-independence resolution, even with GCH: Baumgartner (1984) proved consistency of the required graph's existence with GCH, while Foreman–Laver (1988), relative to a large-cardinal hypothesis, proved consistency with GCH of its nonexistence.
status_issues.evidence: Lambie-Hanson–Rinot, Reflection on the coloring and chromatic numbers, §2.1, https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929, lists both results for an `(ℵ₀, ℵ₂)`-chromatic graph of size ℵ₂. Their definition requires countable chromatic number on all strictly smaller subgraphs. This agrees with the Lean condition at size exactly ℵ₁, because graphs on countably many vertices are automatically countably colorable; this threshold equivalence was also proved in Lean. The cited original results are Baumgartner, Generic graph construction, J. Symbolic Logic 49 (1984), 234–240, and Foreman–Laver, Some downwards transfer properties for ℵ₂, Adv. Math. 67 (1988), 230–238.
status_issues.suggested_change: Record the first part as settled by relative independence, documenting the large-cardinal consistency qualification and references. Following the repository's independence convention, use `research solved` with an explained unresolved truth-value placeholder, rather than assigning `answer(True)` or `answer(False)` as a ZFC answer.

status_issues.source_status: This is equivalent to part i and has the same relative-independence resolution: consistency of existence with GCH by Baumgartner (1984), and relative consistency of nonexistence with GCH by Foreman–Laver (1988).
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06929, §2.1, explicitly lists these opposite consistency results for `(ℵ₀, ℵ₂)`-chromatic graphs of size ℵ₂. The exact-ℵ₁ and all-strictly-smaller formulations agree, and arbitrary versus induced subgraphs are equivalent for the upper bound.
status_issues.suggested_change: Update this variant's status together with `parts.i`, recording relative independence and its consistency assumptions; do not replace the answer placeholder with an unconditional True or False.

reformulations.difference: This variant quantifies over arbitrary `G.Subgraph`s rather than the induced subgraphs used in the 1968 source and in `parts.i`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every arbitrary subgraph H is a spanning subgraph of the induced graph on H.verts, so restricting a coloring gives `H.coe.chromaticCardinal ≤ (G.induce H.verts).chromaticCardinal`. Conversely, the induced graph on any W is the coe of `(⊤ : G.Subgraph).induce W`. Thus the two upper-bound conditions, and the complete existence assertions, are equivalent. Both the general equivalence and its specialization to this part were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: This variant allows arbitrary subgraphs rather than only induced subgraphs, with vertex threshold ℵ_ω.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same coloring-restriction argument works at every cardinal threshold: arbitrary subgraphs have no larger chromatic cardinal than their induced completion, and every induced graph is represented by a top subgraph restricted to its vertex set. The full existence assertions for part ii were proved equivalent in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The file also asserts nonexistence for the induced-subgraph reading of the literal `= ℵ₀` question, although the immediate edgeless-subgraph argument applies only to arbitrary subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The induced version is also impossible. Choose W of size ℵ₁. Its required countable coloring has an independent color class of size ℵ₁, since a countable union of countable sets is countable. The induced graph on that class is edgeless and has chromatic cardinal 1, contradicting the required equality with ℵ₀. The arbitrary-subgraph version is impossible by choosing an edgeless subgraph of size ℵ₁. Both nonexistence statements and their biconditional were proved independently in Lean, without using the target file's sorry theorems.

reformulations.difference: The file extends the literal `= ℵ₀` nonexistence assertion to induced subgraphs of size ℵ_ω.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This induced version is also impossible under its stated ambient cardinalities. Put κ = ℵ_ω. A graph on κ⁺ vertices with chromatic cardinal ℵ₁ is partitioned into ℵ₁ independent color classes. Some class has at least κ vertices: otherwise their union has size at most ℵ₁·κ = κ. Selecting κ vertices from that class yields an edgeless induced graph, contradicting chromatic cardinal ℵ₀. The arbitrary-subgraph version has the immediate edgeless-subgraph contradiction. Both statements and their biconditional were proved independently in Lean.

review.notes: All nine theorem statements were reviewed. The live erdosproblems.com/918 page repeatedly returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its latest wording and annotations could not be read directly. The original cited papers were available. The community database still marks problem 918 as open at the aggregate level; the status entries above concern only the first part and rely on the explicit later literature, not that aggregate label. Part ii is left open. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and contains independent proofs of the four subgraph reformulations, all four textbook nonexistence assertions, the exact-ℵ₁/all-smaller threshold equivalence, and boundary checks. In particular, the chromatic-cardinal infimum is attained because self-coloring makes its defining set nonempty; empty graphs have cardinal 0, nonempty edgeless graphs have cardinal 1, and complete graphs have chromatic cardinal equal to their vertex cardinality. The k = 1 Erdős–Hajnal instance holds, while k = 0 is correctly excluded. The inspected proofs have no sorryAx dependency. No repository files were edited.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported defect is the omission of GCH from a conditional set-theoretic existence theorem. This does not itself furnish a short proof of the unconditional statement or its negation. The k = 1 instance is valid and does not demonstrate the omission; k = 0 is explicitly excluded. No short, honest Lean demonstration of the reported defect is available.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created. The missing-hypothesis finding is supported by the cited source, not by a trivial Lean proof or counterexample.
submission.gave_up_reason: The only reported misformalization concerns a substantive set-theoretic hypothesis. Proving a harmless special case, invoking the target's sorry-backed theorem, or assuming a counterexample would not demonstrate the defect. Establishing the unconditional assertion's truth or failure requires mathematics beyond a short Lean test.

submission.summary: Added an explicit, universe-polymorphic GCH hypothesis while retaining the existing conclusion and positive-k range. Updated the docstring to cite Erdős–Hajnal Corollary 1 and explain the valid k = 1 case. All other declarations are unchanged. The required Lean compile command succeeded with only the permitted `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
